route.name: Specialty Coffee Bar
route.short_description: A quiet counter for espresso, pastries, and slow starts.
route.description: A quiet counter for espresso, pastries, and slow starts. The morning anchor of the recommended route: small batch roasts, warm cardamom buns, and counter seats facing the Altstadt lane.

route.name: Local Bistro
route.short_description: Seasonal plates near Maximilianstraße for an easy midday pause.
route.description: Seasonal plates near Maximilianstraße for an easy midday pause. A compact bistro kitchen with a changing three-course lunch, terrace tables under the linden trees, and a very good house rosé.

route.name: City Gallery
route.short_description: An art stop close to Rathausplatz with compact city-center energy.
route.description: An art stop close to Rathausplatz with compact city-center energy. Contemporary rooms over two floors, a skylit print cabinet, and a ninety-minute route that pairs well with a fountain-side break.

route.name: Rooftop Bar
route.short_description: A skyline drink stop as the city shifts into evening light.
route.description: A skyline drink stop as the city shifts into evening light. Sunset-facing bar tables above the Dom spires, a short spritz list, and the exact moment the towers go gold.

route.name: Garden Restaurant
route.short_description: Garden tables, late dinner plates, and a softer end to the route.
route.description: Garden tables, late dinner plates, and a softer end to the route. A candle-lit courtyard kitchen behind Innenstadt Gasse — the closing table of the recommended day.

sights.name: Fuggerei
sights.short_description: The world's oldest social settlement — quiet lanes, courtyards, and the Fugger bells.
sights.description: Six calm stops for the scenic route begin at the Fuggerei, the 500-year-old social settlement founded by the Fugger family. Walk the lanes, peek into the museum house, and let the courtyard quiet reset the pace of the day.

sights.name: Rathausplatz
sights.short_description: The golden hall, the Perlach tower, and the frescoed facades of the old town.
sights.description: The city's front room: the Renaissance Rathaus with its Golden Hall, the Perlach tower at its shoulder, and frescoed patrician facades framing the square. Best in the late light, best with a coffee.

sights.name: Augsburg Cathedral
sights.short_description: Romanesque-Gothic nave with the oldest figural stained glass in the world.
sights.description: A quiet Gothic stop between the Domviertel lanes. The cathedral holds the oldest surviving figural stained-glass cycle in the world (11th–12th c.) and a bronze door that has opened since 1065 — go early, before the choirs.

sights.name: Perlachturm
sights.short_description: The 70-metre tower lookout over rooftops, onion domes, and the Alps on clear days.
sights.description: The city lookout: 261 steps to a balcony over Augsburg's rooftops, the Dom spires at arm's length, and — on the clearest winter days — the Alps along the horizon.

sights.name: Lech Canals
sights.short_description: The UNESCO water system — mill canals, footbridges, and weavers' houses.
sights.description: A waterfront walk through the UNESCO-listed Augsburg water management system: Lech canals driving medieval mills, red weavers' houses leaning over the water, and footbridges that photograph at any hour.

sights.name: Schaezlerpalais
sights.short_description: A rococo ballroom of mirrors and the state gallery's baroque hang.
sights.description: The baroque gallery stop: a rococo mirror ballroom that opens like a jewellery box onto the Maximilianstraße axis, with the state gallery's baroque hang one corridor away.

restaurants.name: Volta
restaurants.short_description: Charged plates and a short natural list on Innenstadt Gasse.
restaurants.description: Volta plates modern European courses with an electric energy — a counter of ten seats, a four-course arc, and a short natural-wine list that leans local. The featured table of the highlighted route.

restaurants.name: Roux
restaurants.short_description: Classic French reductions, burgundy banquettes, and a solo steak frites.
restaurants.description: Roux does the French classics at a proper pace — hollandaise done tableside, a wine list with Jura depth, and the best solo bar seat in the quarter.

restaurants.name: Aura
restaurants.short_description: Mediterranean plates under a glass atrium — lemons, embers, long lunches.
restaurants.description: Aura brings the Mediterranean north: coal-oven vegetables, whole fish under lemon, and an atrium room that holds afternoon light until six.

restaurants.name: Garbo
restaurants.short_description: Late-shift bistro — martinis, schnitzel, and a jukebox that means it.
restaurants.description: Garbo is the late-shift bistro: one room, one bar, dry martinis, a schnitzel that beats the wine bars at their own game, and a jukebox stocked with conviction.

restaurants.name: Kōan
restaurants.short_description: Edomae counter sushi in an eight-seat room off the Dom lanes.
restaurants.description: Kōan is an eight-seat Edomae counter tucked behind the Dom lanes — aged fish, warm rice, and a pace set by one itamae and two timers.

restaurants.name: Ember
restaurants.short_description: Open-fire grill house — coal signatures, bone marrow, grilled peaches.
restaurants.description: Ember runs an open-fire kitchen: coal-signed vegetables, bone marrow with sourdough, and grilled peaches with pistachio cream for the walk home.

restaurants.name: Silo
restaurants.short_description: Modern Bavarian tasting plates in a converted grain store.
restaurants.description: Silo cooks modern Bavarian in a converted grain store — pretzel sourdough, trout from the Allgäu, and desserts built on bee pollen from the Fuggerei hives.

restaurants.name: Lagom
restaurants.short_description: Nordic small plates, aquavit, and exactly the right amount of dill.
restaurants.description: Lagom translates as 'just enough' and cooks like it: Nordic small plates, aquavit flights, birch-sap granita, and exactly the right amount of dill.

restaurants.name: Noma Sud
restaurants.short_description: Coastal cooking — brine, smoke, and beach-rose sorbet.
restaurants.description: Noma Sud takes the coast inland: brine-cured bass, smoked butter, beach-rose sorbet, and a salt shelf worth reading.

restaurants.name: Canteen No. 7
restaurants.short_description: The workers' canteen gone lovely — one menu, bench tables, fast lunch.
restaurants.description: Canteen No. 7 keeps the workers'-canteen bones and adds a proper kitchen: one daily menu, bench tables, a lunch that lands in twelve minutes flat.

restaurants.name: Terroir
restaurants.short_description: Wine bar with a Franconian heart and a cellar of small growers.
restaurants.description: Terroir pours small-grower Franconian and Swabian bottles with a cheese and bread programme that quietly outclasses restaurants twice its size.

restaurants.name: Pollen
restaurants.short_description: All-day bakery — morning buns, honey from the city hives, quince turnovers.
restaurants.description: Pollen is the all-day bakery: morning buns at seven, honey from the city hives, quince turnovers at four, and a line that moves.

restaurants.name: Soot
restaurants.short_description: Dark bar kitchen — charcoal bread,Highball pour, and vinyl till late.
restaurants.description: Soot is the dark-room bar kitchen: charcoal bread with cultured butter, a highball programme that never misses, and vinyl till the legal limit.

restaurants.name: Velvet Room
restaurants.short_description: A twenty-seat supper club behind a curtain — one seating, one menu.
restaurants.description: Velvet Room is a twenty-seat supper club behind a curtain on Annstraße: one seating, one menu, one host, and a room that talks back.

restaurants.name: Granary
restaurants.short_description: Swabian rösthaus in the old granary — spätzle, maultaschen, dark beer.
restaurants.description: Granary keeps the old granary beams and cooks Swabian underneath them: cheese spätzle from a copper pan, maultaschen in broth, and dark beer from the copper kettle.

restaurants.name: Faro
restaurants.short_description: Lighthouse grill room — whole birds, ember vegetables, and custard pies.
restaurants.description: Faro is the lighthouse grill room: whole birds over ember, vegetables that taste of the fire, and custard pies sliced to order at the counter.
